0.clinical_summary: The deep learning model detected radiological patterns characteristic of a Cystine Kidney Stone or Renal Cystic formation within the kidney parenchyma.
0.description: Cystine stones are a metabolic form of urolithiasis caused by cystinuria, resulting in high concentrations of insoluble cystine crystals in the urinary tract. In CT imaging, these manifest as persistent hyperdense or well-circumscribed cystic structures.
treatments: Hydration Regimen: Aggressive fluid intake (>3.5 to 4 liters/day) to maintain urine output above 3 L/day.
Urinary Alkalinization: Administration of potassium citrate or sodium bicarbonate to maintain urinary pH between 7.0 and 7.5 (dramatically increasing cystine solubility).
Dietary Adjustments: Restrict dietary sodium (<2,000 mg/day) and moderate animal protein intake to decrease cystine excretion.
Thiol-Binding Pharmacotherapy: Tiopronin (Thiola) or D-penicillamine if urinary cystine excretion remains >500 mg/day despite alkalinization.

Surgical / Interventional Management: Extracorporeal Shock Wave Lithotripsy (ESWL) often has reduced efficacy on hard cystine stones; Ureteroscopy (URS) with holmium laser or Percutaneous Nephrolithotomy (PCNL) is preferred for stones >15 mm.

1.status_badge: Normal Scan - No Pathological Abnormalities Detected
1.clinical_summary: No signs of nephrolithiasis, calculi, renal masses, or suspicious cystic abnormalities detected.
1.description: The renal cortex, medulla, pelvicalyceal system, and surrounding perinephric fat planes demonstrate normal anatomical continuity with no radio-opaque calculi or atypical density variations.
treatments: Optimal Hydration: Continue drinking 2.0 to 2.5 liters of clean water daily to preserve optimal renal clearance.
Dietary Balance: Maintain a balanced diet rich in citrus fruits, moderate calcium, and low refined salts.
Kidney Function Monitoring: Routine annual preventative checkups including serum creatinine, BUN, and urinalysis.
Lifestyle Maintenance: Regular cardiovascular exercise and blood pressure regulation to protect microvascular nephron integrity.

2.status_badge: Critical Finding - Urgent Urological / Oncological Referral
2.clinical_summary: The model detected structural heterogeneity, parenchymal deformation, and density shifts indicative of a renal mass or neoplastic lesion.
2.description: Renal tumors may encompass renal cell carcinoma (RCC), oncocytoma, or angiomyolipoma. Accurate early radiological recognition is paramount for organ-sparing intervention and favorable prognosis.
treatments: Urgent Urological Consultation: Immediate referral to a specialized urologic surgeon or multidisciplinary oncology tumor board.
Multiphasic Contrast CT / MRI: Quad-phase contrast-enhanced abdominal CT or renal MRI protocol to evaluate contrast enhancement, vascular involvement, and renal vein thrombosis.
Surgical Resection: Partial Nephrectomy (nephron-sparing surgery for T1a/T1b tumors) or Radical Nephrectomy depending on mass diameter and RENAL nephrometry score.
Thermal Ablation Options: Percutaneous cryoablation or microwave ablation for select small renal masses (<3 cm) in high-surgical-risk patients.
Histopathology & Staging: Post-surgical pathology for Fuhrman/WHO nuclear grading, staging, and potential systemic/targeted therapy if indicated.
